page.layout: One page of running text in one column; margin notes left ("Incolæ", "Familiæ nobiles") and right (numerals 10, 20, 30, 40, 50); below the text a four-column list of family names in italic; running head at top.

main_text.p: nus XLIII, Ioannes Barbus XLIIII, Paullus Fuscarus XLV, Ioannes Amadeus XLVI, Angelus Cavarius XLVII, Ioannes Lauredanus XLVIII, Franciscus Faletrus XLIX, Leonardus Delphinus L, Franciscus Bembus LI, Marcus Landus LII, Franciscus Mariopetrus LIII, Laurentius Iustinianus LIV, & ultimus, Primus, ut ante dixi, Patriarcha creatus anno cIↄ CCCCLI. Alibi Antistites fuerunt Henricus Contarenus, Castelli; Dominicus Dominicus & Petrus Aemilianus, Vicentiæ; Fantinus, Patavij; Petrus Montens, Brixiæ; Iacobus Zeno, Feltrij Bellunique; Dominicus, Torcelli. Inter Duces eruditionis etiam laudem consecuti Andreas Dandalus, qui insignem scripsit historiam; Karolus Zeno, & alij. Iurisconsultos dederunt Venetiæ Marcum Lippamanum, Barbonum Mauroce-num, Ludovicum Fuscarum, Vitalem Landum, Candianum Polanum, Nicolaum Canalem, Laurum Quirinum: Historiographum, Andream Navagerium: Oratores; Zacchariam Trevisanum, Leonardum Iustinianum, Franciscum Farbarum, Hieronymum Donatum, Hieronymum Georgium, Equitem Auratum: Polyhistores; Manutios & Io. Baptistam Egnatium: Poetas, Andream Maurocenum, Hermolaum Donatum, & alios. Nusquam autem plures, qui rei bellicæ scientia gloriam sibi conciliarunt immortalem. Ex iis, qui maximis potiti victoriis nomen Venetum terra marique plurimum auxerunt, memorantur cum primis Ioannes & Raynus Polani, Marinus Grandonicus, Dominicus Maurocenus, Ioannes Basilius, Thomas Falerius, Reinherus Dandulus, Rugerius Permarinus, Ioannes Trevisanus, Petrus Thomas Ioannes Grittus, Nicolaus Balestrerius, Marcus Bonus, Andreas Tocanus, Leonardus Quirinus, Marcus Onisforus, Rainerus Zeno, Laurentius Theupolus; Andreas Zeno, Marcus Gradonicus, Marcus Michael, Gilbertus Dandalus, Iacobus Dandalus, Ruggerius Maurocenus, Ioannes Superantius, Benedictus Iustinianus, Petrus Zeno, qui primus omnium Dux in Turcas ab Venetis ivit: Successores nactus Marinum Falerium, Andream Co[ntarenum], Petrum & Marcum Canales, & Marcum Iustinianum. Addendi Andreas Maurocenus, Simon Dandalus, Nicolaus Gradonicus, Pancratius Iustinianus. Summam laudem Classis Præfecturæ meruerunt Nicolaus Pisanus, Ioannes Delphinus, Paullus Lauredanus, Marcus Michael, Ioannes Sanutus, Marcus Cornelius, Bernhardus Iustinianus, Dominicus Michael, Crespus Molinus, Michael Delphinus, Iacobus Maurus, Marcus Iustinianus, Karolus Zeno, Michael Iustinianus, Petrus Hemus, Fantinus Georgius, Marcus Grimanus, Ioannes Barbus, Victor Fabius, Franciscus Bembus, Petrus Lauredanus, Andreas Mocenicus, Stephanus Contarenus, Aloysius Lauredanus, Victor Capellus, Vrsatus Iustinianus, Iacobus Lauredanus, Nicolaus Canalis, Petrus Mocenicus, Hieronymus Canalis, Vincentius Capellus, Andreas Trevisanus, Eques Auratus, Laurentius Amulius, & alij. Civium frequentia Venetijs plane stupenda. Numerus trecentorum circiter millium censetur. Triplicis illi sunt generis: Patritij, quos penes Imperij & Reip. administratio; Cives, qui Scribarum & aliorum honorum munera gerunt; Artifices, qui mechanicas exercent Artes. Præter hos, Mercatores ibi innumeri & advenæ, qui vario cultu ex omnibus mundi partibus negociationis gratia confluere soliti: Turcæ, Æthiopes, Slavi, Arabes, Syri, Cretenses, Cyprij, Macedones, Germani, Vngari, Hispani, Galli, alij. page.notes: Margin notes: left "Incolæ" beside the paragraph on civium frequentia; left "Familiæ nobiles" beside the closing sentence. Right-margin numerals 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 are line counters, not text. Words in the list and the left-margin notes are partly doubtful; the printed page is faint and some letters, notably in the Greek-named and Venetian names, are uncertain. Mauroceni at the foot is a catchword-like addition.
